newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan June oil product imports fall on high output.
newsitem.headline: Japan June oil product imports fall on high output.

text.p: Brisk domestic production and high inventories weighed on Japan's oil product imports in June, oil product traders said on Tuesday.

Japan's domestic oil product output in June grew 9.4 percent from a year earlier to 16.25 million kl, while imports totalled 2.94 million kl, down 9.3 percent on the year, Trade Ministry data released on Tuesday showed.
Oil product stocks at the end of June stood at 13.95 million kl, an increase of 11 percent from a year earlier.
The rise marked a year-on-year increase for the eleventh consecutive month in June, a trade ministry official said.
Traders said high domestic inventories had dampened imports of kerosene and gas oil, which were down by 74 percent and 78.8 percent respectively from a year earlier.
Imports of grade-C fuel oil, which is mainly used to fuel thermal power generators and ships, also fell by 31.6 percent from June 1996 levels to 208,000 kl.

Kerosene imports are believed to have bottomed out in June and are expected to pick up gradually towards the winter as oil firms and trading houses start to pile up stocks for the peak heating season in the winter, traders said.
